components.css: .ds-star { position: relative; width: 0; height: 0; margin: 60px; } .ds-star-core { position: absolute; left: -25px; top: -25px; width: 50px; height: 50px; border-radius: 999px; display: grid; place-items: center; color: var(--ink, #f2f0ea); background: radial-gradient(circle at 35% 30%, rgb(255 255 255 / 0.14), rgb(8 10 22 / 0.92) 70%); border: 1px solid rgb(255 255 255 / 0.18); box-shadow: 0 10px 26px -10px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.9); transition: color 0.35s cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1), border-color 0.35s cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1), transform 0.45s cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1), box-shadow 0.45s cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1); } .ds-star:hover .ds-star-core { color: var(--brand); border-color: color-mix(in srgb, var(--brand) 70%, white); transform: scale(1.14); box-shadow: 0 0 28px -2px color-mix(in srgb, var(--brand) 55%, transparent); } .ds-star-halo { position: absolute; left: -42px; top: -42px; width: 84px; height: 84px; border-radius: 999px; background: radial-gradient(circle, color-mix(in srgb, var(--brand) 32%, transparent) 0%, transparent 66%); animation: ds-twinkle 3.2s ease-in-out infinite; pointer-events: none; } .ds-star-flare { position: absolute; left: -48px; top: -48px; width: 96px; height: 96px; color: rgb(255 255 255 / 0.55); opacity: 0; transform: scale(0.4) rotate(0deg); transition: opacity 0.4s cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1), transform 0.7s cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1); pointer-events: none; } .ds-star:hover .ds-star-flare { opacity: 0.9; transform: scale(1) rotate(45deg); } .ds-star-label { position: absolute; top: 33px; left: 0; transform: translateX(-50%); white-space: nowrap; font: 13px 'Geist Variable', system-ui, sans-serif; color: var(--ink-dim, #b9bcc7); transition: color 0.3s; } .ds-star:hover .ds-star-label { color: var(--ink, #f2f0ea); } @keyframes ds-twinkle { 0%, 100% { opacity: 0.35; transform: scale(0.85); } 50% { opacity: 1; transform: scale(1.12); } } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-star-halo { animation: none; } }

narrative.overview:
The page is a real flight through the solar system, and the story is painted directly onto the window. Near-black space carries a live WebGL scene (NASA-derived planet maps lit by one sun, a real Milky Way, a drifting astronaut), and every word sits straight on that space. Legibility comes from a directional darkening that falls off toward the planet, never from a box, card or glass panel. One body per chapter; the visitor's scroll is the camera's burn from one world to the next.

Two voices share the frame. Permanent Marker is the human one: huge, loaded with paint, revealing left to right like a single brush stroke, with an amber swash dragged under the biggest lines. Geist and Geist Mono are the instrument: calm body copy, uppercase telemetry labels, hairline rows. A layer of playful marks (rotated stickers on the name, a live signal chip with breathing bars, a trailing amber cursor ring, constellations of brand-logo stars) adds Gen-Z energy without breaking the realism, because each of them behaves like light or like a sticker on a visor, not like UI furniture.

Density is low and cinematic. Each chapter's content is budgeted to fit one desktop viewport on its own side of the screen, alternating left and right so the planet always has the other half.
keyCharacteristics: Text sits directly on space over a side-falloff scrim; no boxed panels.
One accent: sunlight amber. Signal green means "live" and nothing else.
Brush display type at poster scale; mono uppercase labels as telemetry.
Light pill as the one primary action per view; hairline outline for the rest.
Motion is the journey: paint-in headlines, drawn swashes and lines, twinkling stars, a single ease-out curve.

rules.name: The One Sun Rule
rules.body: Amber is the only accent hue in the interface. Brand colours from skill logos appear only inside a hovered skill star; planet atmospheres belong to the 3D scene, not the UI.

rules.name: The Live Light Rule
rules.body: Signal green marks something that is live or current right now. If it is not live, it is not green.

rules.name: The Paint-In Rule
rules.body: Every brush headline reveals left to right with a clip-path sweep and a 14px drift (1.25s, ease-out), as one loaded stroke. Body copy never paints; it rises.

rules.name: The Brush Is For Voices Rule
rules.body: Permanent Marker is for headlines, the wordmark, mobile-menu chapter links and short asides. Never for paragraphs, labels, buttons or data.

rules.name: The Scrim Not Box Rule
rules.body: Legibility comes from a directional gradient behind the column, never from a container with a background and border.

rules.name: The Only Light Glows Rule
rules.body: A glow is reserved for something that is a light: a star, a pulse, a live status. Buttons, chips and text never glow.

dos: Do set every text column directly on space over the side-falloff scrim (0.82 / 0.7 / 0 at 66%), alternating sides chapter by chapter.
Do keep amber (flare) the only interface accent; use it as strokes, underlines, edges and hover states.
Do reserve signal green for live or current status.
Do paint brush headlines in with the left-to-right clip reveal and let body copy rise 18px after it, on the single ease-out curve `cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)`.
Do keep one light pill per view and make every other action an outline pill.
Do carry data as hairline rows with mono uppercase labels, not as cards.
Do give every looping animation (twinkle, dust, bars, scroll cue, pulses, auto-cycle) a still state under `prefers-reduced-motion`, and keep the page complete without it.
Do budget each chapter's content to fit one desktop viewport.
donts: Don't put text in boxed panels, cards or glass surfaces; the only surface allowed is the mobile menu sheet.
Don't introduce a second accent hue in the interface or use brand logo colours outside a hovered skill star.
Don't glow buttons, chips or type; glows belong to stars, pulses and live status.
Don't set paragraphs, labels or buttons in Permanent Marker.
Don't use pure white for text; ink is warm bone.
Don't use ink-faint for running body copy; it is for labels only.
Don't render planets as flat, cartoon or toy illustrations; bodies are real lit maps in the WebGL scene.
